name: He Who Fights With Monsters | Complete Lorebook (Books 1-13)
description: A comprehensive lorebook for the He Who Fights With Monsters LitRPG series (Shirtaloon), covering Books 1-13: world and magic system, essences, ranks, gods and great astral beings, characters, places, organisations, artefacts and per-book story events up to the end of Book 13. Book text takes precedence over the fan wiki where they conflict. Spoilers throughout.

1.content: Pallimustus is the magic-rich twin of Earth: an alternate version of Earth created from the same universe-seed template, with similar but warped continents (Africa disconnected from Eurasia, a SE Asian landmass pushing into Australia and NZ, no Iberia or Arabia so the Mediterranean joins the Indian Ocean via the Gramid Passage; Sri Lanka-like Pranay huge). Horse-equivalent: heidels (two-headed scaled horned work animals). Two moons (one is the Mystic Moon governing tides). Calendar: 12 months of 30 days + 5 extra days (solstice/equinox/new year); six-day week (Fourthday, Fifthday...); the year begins in spring. Its dimensional membrane is thin, so ambient magic is dense, astral spaces (pocket dimensions) are attached to the planet, and monsters, essences and awakening stones manifest naturally. Natives call the world 'the world'; the name Pallimustus was learned from Dawn's painting. A monster surge happens roughly every ~10 years (8-13). Major regions: Estercost (Vitesse, Cyrion, Greenstone), the Storm Kingdom (Rimaros), Yaresh (elf rainforest), Kurdansk/Dreisil, Sadi Andali, Girlano, Pranay (Jayapura), the Dragon Lands, the Great Southern Continent.
1.name: Pallimustus (the world)

2.content: Earth: thicker dimensional membrane than Pallimustus (reinforced by the World-Phoenix billions of years ago) so it began as magic-poor (affinity gems = quintessence; mana lamps; no monsters). A link built ~500 years ago (by the Network founder with a Builder-door and a Pallimustus deity's help) siphoned magic from Pallimustus to Earth; the Network's Grid intercepted proto-astral spaces. Sabotage of the Grid (EOA) triggered monster waves, transformation zones (alien landscapes, population transformed into other races), and direct manifestation of monsters, essences and awakening stones once density crossed the iron threshold. Jason repaired the link nodes in Books 5-6; Earth in 2038 has lower magic than Pallimustus, with spirit coin farms, magitech, fossil fuels abandoned, vampires hunted, EDJI formed. Time is synchronised with Pallimustus by the link. Earth and Pallimustus are metaphysically 'the same planet' which lets Knowledge cross.
2.name: Earth (the world) differences

3.content: The System: originally Jason's personal outworlder interface (quests, inventory, character sheet, map, party). In Book 11 Jason repaired and sat on the Cosmic Throne: every essence-user in the cosmos sees 'Don't Panic. Everything is going to be fine. Welcome to the System.' Jason is its [System Administrator] (he is the great astral being behind it; if he dies, it persists as an imprint of his echo on the Cosmic Throne). It identifies rank, progress, abilities, boons/afflictions, party/raid voice chat and tactical maps; evolves to include species gift evolutions; unchanged cores (Power/Speed/Spirit/Recovery attributes). He can switch it off in regions (Book 12: slave-law regions lost System access for ~1 day notice). Some people see it as an affront to religion; a few died killing to keep it from the oppressed. Gods have no say in his realm.
3.name: The System

4.content: Essences are manifestations of pure magic that act on and shape the latent power of the soul. Rarities: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary (no essence is absolutely better: a duck can beat a fox). A person absorbs up to four essences via ritual (the fourth often a confluence); each essence provides five essence abilities, one awakened on absorption and the rest via awakening stones. Rank-up requires all essences full and abilities at the next rank. Essence ability rank-ups raise the matching attribute (Power/Speed/Spirit/Recovery). Divine essences from gods stay connected to the god and can be revoked. Awakening happens ~16-17 (Rufus waited till 19; Emi at ~15-16). Essences resonate with existing aspects of identity (blood found violence, dark found deception, sin found a god-position). Essences are 'the shape; the soul is the power'. Essence abilities come in types: special attacks, spells, special abilities, auras, conjurations, familiars, summons, rituals. See also: Awakening Stones, Confluence Essences, Quintessence.
4.name: Essences

5.content: A confluence essence manifests after three essences are absorbed; if refused there is no replacement. In Books 1-10 confluence outcomes were fixed per combination (the Magic Society's living tablet catalogues thousands). After the Cosmic Throne was sundered the Celestial Book locked each combination to one confluence; as Jason repaired the Throne (from Book 11, first seen at Emi's ritual: Vast+Myriad+Harmonic gave Resonant not Unity) combinations vary again. Examples: Dark+Blood+Sin = Doom (affliction specialist; Jason, Itsuki Tiwari); Earth+Fire+Potent = Volcano (Farrah); Magic+Might+Wing = Dragon (Humphrey); Swift+Balance+Wind = Mystic (Sophie); Magic+Trap+Adept = Charlatan (Belinda); Shield+Growth+Renewal = Prosperity (Neil); Rune+Magic+Balance+Karmic (Clive: Karmic gives Mantle of Retribution/Eye of Karma); Blood+Death+X = Undeath (restricted); Sin+X = Succubus (restricted); Sacrifice (restricted); Feast+Knife+Dance = Bounty (Erika); Renewal+Life+Pure = Ministration (Ian); Vehicle+Wind+Swift = Soaring (Kaito); Might+Swift+Bird/Wing = Garuda (Taika); Sword+Adept+Magic = Master (Akari); Hammer+Fire+Iron+Forge (Gary).
5.name: Confluence Essences

6.comment: Restricted essences and the Magic Society tablet
6.content: Restricted essences (usually confluences) are those the Adventure Society deems dangerous to the public: Death, Corrupt, Sacrifice, Undeath, Succubus and others (the Society offers rewards for [Death] and [Corrupt] essences and puts out contracts on users). The Magic Society's 'living document' marble-and-gold tablet lists known essences and combinations; a Greenstone fighter had the Sacrifice confluence. Doom (Jason's) is unrestricted.
6.name: Restricted essences and the Magic Society tablet

7.content: Awakening stones awaken essence abilities. Common stones give a wide pool, rarer stones are narrower and more specific; rarities 1-5 stars (Common to Legendary); the essence is the biggest determinant of the ability; race, knowledge (e.g., ritual magic) and personality influence it. Created like essences/monsters; gods and astral beings also grant them (divine stones can be revoked; astral gifts cannot). AS rule: no stones for killing monsters above your rank. Notable stones in Jason's build: Stars (Cloak of Night), Adventure (Path of Shadows), Feast (Leech Bite, Feast of Blood, Feast of Absolution, Sin Eater), Apocalypse (Sanguine Horror), Omens (Hegemony), Wrath (Punition), Magus (Castigate, Haemorrhage), Absolution (Blade of Doom), Judgement (Verdict), Avatar (Avatar of Doom), Reaper (Shadow of the Reaper, Hand of the Reaper, Avatar of Doom), Inevitability (Inevitable Demise).
7.name: Awakening Stones (system)

8.content: Quintessence: unranked pieces of an essence that cannot be assembled into a complete essence; used in rituals, alchemy, weapon-forging and fuel for magical items (e.g., water quintessence in the Oasis Bracelet). On Earth it is called affinity gems. Myriad quintessence is multiplicative for crafting. Cloud flask upgrades need air/water/dimension quintessence.
8.name: Quintessence (system)

9.content: Ranks: normal -> iron -> bronze -> silver -> gold -> diamond -> transcendent. On Earth the Network calls them categories 0-5 (Cabal: tiers). Higher ranks suppress lower ranks ('tyranny of rank'); individuals fighting higher ranks have disadvantages. Rank-up: all four essence slots filled and all abilities at the next rank (iron needs all four stones/essences; silver->gold needs every ability gold, plus 'essence revelations' for gold; gold->diamond needs insight and rarely core users). Lifespans: normal ~60-75 (average), iron ~75+, bronze ~100+, silver ~200, gold ~500 and no need to breathe, diamond ageless; transcendent unkillable. Iron: no need to eat/drink (spirit coins), DR vs mundane damage, sense auras, body purge. Bronze: all abilities at bronze; Silver: attribute walls, flight by aura (levitation), a killing blow no longer kills; Gold: can't be easily killed, can't resurrect from non-grace; Diamond: ageless, 'once one reaches diamond many old rules stop applying'; half-transcendent = peak diamond + transcended mortality; a diamond who transcends becomes a god-level being. Monsters also have ranks by quality of magic. Monster cores speed advancement (humans fastest) but halt it by silver and make gold nearly impossible.
9.name: Ranks

10.content: Four base attributes: Power, Speed, Spirit, Recovery, each tied to essences by ability level (Jason: Power=Blood, Speed=Dark, Spirit=Doom, Recovery=Sin). Past bronze, Spirit enhances senses. Wall at silver 4 requires insight, not just training.
10.name: Attributes

11.content: An aura is a physical yet intangible extension of the soul/will; it grows with rank, can be projected, restrained, suppressed (only vs weaker auras) and used for emotion pressure, levitation (silver), perception and physical force at higher ranks (messengers use it to manipulate matter). Gold auras are felt by anyone nearby; uncontrolled auras of high-rank people hurt the unranked (aura suppressor items). Aura masks/beacons (messenger tech) fake or block auras. Essence aura abilities (Hegemony, Cleansing Breeze, Dragon's Might, Unbowed, Spoils of Victory...). Title effects: Godless Prophet, Giant Slayer, Resolute, Indomitable, Spirit Warrior, Reality Hegemon, Keeper of the Cycle. Isolation (duel) powers of messengers suppress all powers.
11.name: Auras (system)

12.content: Every nature/race has six inherent racial gifts (which can evolve once with a blessing from a great astral being, and a second time in rare cases). Essence-capable natures: Human (Special Attack Aptitude, Human Ambition...), Elf (life/nature/magic affinity), Leonid (stronger/faster), Celestine (astral & holy affinity; metallic hair/eyes; offspring of two outworlders; best portal users), Draconian (scales, fire breath, claim dragon descent), Smoulder (earth+fire), Runic (blue-black skin with glowing runes), Merfolk, Goblin, Valash (Earth transformation victims), Lehenik (Jason's soul people), Outworlder (Interface, Quest System, Inventory, Map, Astral Affinity, Mysterious Stranger -> later transfigured), Messengers (not essence-capable). Jason's racial list evolved: Party Interface, Defiant, Spirit Vault/Domain, Tactical Map, Nirvanic Transfiguration, Dark Rider; with the prime avatar these were replaced by 'nature' gifts.
12.name: Natures and Races

13.content: Monsters are magic made sentient without a soul; they appear from high ambient magic, last days to weeks (lesser 1-2 weeks, iron ~1 month, higher longer; aggressive near the end), and dissolve into rainbow smoke leaving loot (cores, coins, ointments, items). Rank is the quality of their magic. A monster surge is a world's cyclical pressure release: ambient magic spikes drastically, monsters, essences and stones flood out like a sluice gate. On Pallimustus surges come roughly every ~10 years; the Earth link delayed the last one by ~15 years, so the Builder-era surge in Book 7 was huge (diamond-rank monsters appear). Tyranny of rank and 'monster notices' (Adventure Society boards) govern hunts. Intelligent monsters are born with knowledge.
13.name: Monsters and Monster Surges

14.content: Saturation = quantity of magic in a region (more frequent manifestations); density = quality (the rank of manifestations). Greenstone's density is mid-iron with low saturation; Vitesse is silver; the Jungle astral space was bronze; Earth after the Grid failed rose to bronze-silver in zones. Low-magic desolation zones cut recovery (stamina -50%, health -75%, mana -99%) and need spirit coins. Surges temporarily raise saturation.
14.name: Ambient Magic: Saturation and Density

15.content: Gods are entities outside physical reality (not quite in the astral between universes), each a concept (Dominion, Healer, Knowledge...), who can manifest avatars and speak with Akashic Speech. They give followers essences and awakening stones (revocable). Major gods (Ocean, Storm, War, Knowledge) govern wide domains; minor gods (Farmer, Mason, Grocer, Hygiene) serve major gods or act alone; evil/hidden gods are worshipped in secret (Deceit, Destruction, Pain, Undeath, Discord). Known gods: Champion, Chastity, Death, Deceit, Deep, Desolate, Destruction, Discord, Disguise, Dominion, Earth, Fertility, Guardian, Healer, Hearth, Hero, Journey, Justice, Knowledge, Liberty, Lust, Merchant, Ocean, Pain, Purity, Refuge, Revels, Rivers, Roads, Slavery, Soldier, Stone, Storm, Strength, Subtlety, Trade, Truth, Undeath, Vengeance, Vineyard, War, Warrior, Wind, plus Farmer, Mason, Grocer, Hygiene, Architect, Gardener. Gods cannot enter another god's dominion (but followers can conquer and claim), cannot enter Jason's realm, cannot affect his mind in spirit domains, and cannot reveal other gods' deceptions. Gods do not rule worlds like the Cosmic Throne; they can be sanctioned. Followers' deaths are tallied by the Church of Death. Gods' unilateral decree: none may interfere with the search for Purity's artefact.
15.name: Gods (overview)

16.content: Great astral beings (GABs) are cosmic-scale transcendents (aspects of the cosmos) who generate authority; they operate via prime vessels/avatars; their true state is mindless-alien but they enjoy mortal bodies; some are venerated like gods. Named: World-Phoenix (dimensional integrity; formerly the Boundary), the Builder (construction/forging reality; the new Builder is Zithis Carrow Vayel, a former messenger raised at 16), the Reaper (finality of death), the Keeper of Moments/Sands (time), the All-Devouring Eye (entropy/annihilation), Celestial Book (understanding magic's nature; Clive venerates it), Seeker of Songs, Whisper in Corners, Legion (life), Word in the Silence, plus nameless functionaries (life, death, time, matter) unbound without the Cosmic Throne. Their pacts replaced the Cosmic Throne after they sundered it. Hierophants are former prime vessels.
16.name: Great Astral Beings

17.comment: Cosmos: astral, deep astral, dumpling soup
17.content: Clive's model: the cosmos is dumpling soup - worlds are dumplings, the astral is the soup, the source of all magic; astral spaces are congealed magic attached to a world; the deep astral is pure magic where physical bodies cannot survive (hence the 'outworlder' body of Jason is a familiar-like manifestation). The original Builder crafted twin universe seeds (Earth and Pallimustus) from a chimera singularity. Universes are 'seeds' that germinate; astral kings become miniature universes. Interstice is the universe-city at the cosmic centre. The fundamental realm underlies physical reality (node space: cubes; reality cores are batteries). Transformation zones are scabs over dimensional ulcers.
17.name: Cosmos: astral, deep astral, dumpling soup

18.content: Astral spaces are pocket dimensions attached to the planet through apertures (often waterfalls, caves or portals); they hold monsters and treasure and are tapped for spirit-coin farms. Proto-astral spaces (Earth: 'dimensional incursions') form briefly (43 hours baseline) with an anchor monster; killing it ends them; failing injects monsters into the world. The Builder's cult tried to steal astral spaces; astral spaces can be artificial (the Reaper trials one was a Builder boarding vessel).
18.name: Astral Spaces and Proto-Astral Spaces

19.comment: Rules of Intrusion, pacts and cosmic law
19.content: Rules of Intrusion (old but flexible until the Throne was restored): on entering worlds that have not declared themselves open to the cosmic community; invasions need an invitation and conditions. After Book 11 they are rigid: breaking them triggers consequences. The pacts between GABs (compact between Builder, Reaper, World-Phoenix) restrict direct meddling.
19.name: Rules of Intrusion, pacts and cosmic law

20.content: Sanctioning is an extreme change in a transcendent being's nature through a shift of authority, typically punitive (gods/GABs team up to punish a peer). The old Builder was sanctioned and painted over by a new Builder (the old one still exists beneath); Purity sanctioned himself by pouring his authority into an artefact; Shade sanctioned himself into the Shadow of the Hegemon; Hero sanctioned himself; the World-Phoenix sanctioned the Boundary into herself. Only a god can sanction a god ('you don't kill gods, you sanction them').
20.name: Sanctioning

21.content: Authority is fundamental power (flesh, blood and soul of great astral beings; currency in the cosmos). Will is an active force developed by aura training. Intrinsic-mandate magic is high-order transcendent magic that shapes physical reality by decree. Authority in set-state (put to purpose) vs potential-state (raw). Gordon unlocked orrery rituals of intrinsic-mandate magic.
21.name: Authority, Will and Intrinsic-Mandate Magic

22.content: Soul engineering is transcendent-level craft (the disembodied-soul sword of Greenstone's dungeon; Zolit Kreen; Hallas; Nik; Arbour). Soul forges normally form inside an astral king; Jason acquired one in Book 11. Soul scars are permanent; messengers and Jason are gestalts (body/soul fused). Healing magic uses the soul as blueprint; resurrection works only within an hour of death at gold healing and fails on gestalts. Soul attacks bypass defences.
22.name: Souls and Soul Engineering

23.content: Death/resurrection: the soul lingers with the body from seconds to an hour; gold-rank healers can reverse death in the grace period; untethered souls drift into the astral and can become outworlders. Great astral beings could resurrect minions as outworlders but the Reaper and World-Phoenix object. The Reaper then incited gods to change magic so resurrection got harder (minutes at gold). The Death goddess's pact bars Jason from resurrecting others. Jason's own resurrection tools: World-Phoenix token (consumed Book 3), Nirvanic Transfiguration (once per rank), Star Phoenix state (Book 5-6; he needed an absorbed diamond), Sacred Phoenix gift (Book 12+). Reincarnation (Velius, Reaper): a soul renews as a different person.
23.name: Resurrection lore

24.content: Currency: spirit coins (lesser, iron, bronze, silver, gold, diamond); 100 lesser = 1 iron, then x10 per rank; a gold coin ~100,000 lesser; ranked users can eat a coin of their rank to restore resources; consuming a higher coin raises attributes temporarily with backlash. Spirit coin farms in low-magic regions are a major economy (Greenstone's largest export, Geller-Seven, Mercer farms). Looted coins carry Jason's thumbs-up face ('PRODUCT OF JASON / G'DAY MATE').
24.name: Spirit Coins and Currency

25.content: Adventure Society: global monster-hunting and contract organisation; badges (medallion with sword and rod over a shield) track kills and locate the body; stars rate judgement not power (1-3 stars; 2 = unsupervised responsibility and leading small one-star teams; 3 = politics; stars drop when rank rises). Contract types: boards (notices), contracts, orders (surge rules). Field assessments (monthly) by instructors (Vincent Trenslow, Guy Spalding...). Directors are political appointees. Guilds (Burning Violet, Sapphire Crown...) receive 60% of surge quotas. Continental Council audits branches. Jason's badges: 3 stars (pentagrams) and John Miller 1 star; later gold badge with diamond symbol.
25.name: Adventure Society (system)

26.content: Magic Society: records essences, regulates spirit coin farms (politically neutral), runs water-link communication, magical research and the 'living document'. Greenstone director was Lucian Lamprey (corrupt), then Pochard Finn. The Rakesh campus houses it and the Continental Council. In the Yaresh era an aristocratic faction used it for control. Rivals: Magical Research Association (open).
26.name: Magic Society (system)

27.content: Notable places: Estercost (kingdom; capital Cyrion, largest city; Vitesse city of flowers with Remore Academy and Burning Violet; Greenstone colony; Kazlahk sandstone coastal city with medical university); Storm Kingdom (Rimaros; Sea of Storms); Yaresh (elf rainforest city); Rakesh (north coast; Continental Council); Hornis (port); Boko (desert academic city); Zartos (celestine-heavy subterranean city on a river); Kurdansk (People's Holy Federation of Dreisil; Sophie's birthplace); Pranay (Sri Lanka-like; Jayapura); Girlano (cartel-ruled inland nation); Sadi Andali (lawless slave-market desert nation); Dragon Lands (Antarctic-equivalent); Segurado (Uruguay-equivalent city-state); Jaitari (largest city of the Storm Kingdom on its central island); Isart (Emir's contest site), Cartise (ruined river city), Jorganis (Pacific-equivalent lawless island).
27.name: Geography of the Known World

28.content: Dark [Speed]: Midnight Eyes - iron see through darkness; bronze sense magic; silver read auras; gold diminish light sources. Cloak of Night - iron cloak manipulates light and weight; bronze intercepts projectiles; silver flight and minor space distortion; gold void portal cloak. Path of Shadows - iron shadow teleport; bronze regional portals; silver continental; gold global portals; Shadow Gate (bronze). Hand of the Reaper - iron shadow arm with Creeping Death; bronze + Rigor Mortis, 2nd arm; silver + Weakness of the Flesh, ranged; gold more arms armed with conjured weapons. Shadow of the Hegemon (Shade) - iron 3 bodies; bronze 7 (store items, force); silver 31 (share non-combat powers); gold 211 (beacons). Creeping Death = necrotic disease DoT; Rigor Mortis = penalty to Speed/Recovery; Weakness of the Flesh negates disease/necrotic immunity.
28.name: Jason's Dark essence abilities (full progression)

29.content: Blood [Power]: Blood Harvest (spell: drain life force from recently dead bloods; iron single corpse, bronze area, silver Blood Frenzy/Blood of the Immortal, gold Strength of My Enemies/Endless Power; 'As your life was mine to reap, so your death is mine to harvest'). Leech Bite (special attack: Bleeding, Leech Toxin, Tainted Meridians, Thief of Life). Feast of Blood (spell: drains bleeding targets; bronze extra per poison; silver variant; gold Blood Glutton; 'Your blood is not yours to keep, but mine on which to feast'). Sanguine Horror (familiar Colin: iron familiar; bronze worm-that-walks; silver robes and biomass heal; gold exceed mass limits). Haemorrhage (spell: Bleeding + Sacrificial Victim; Necrotoxin; Blood From a Stone; Exsanguination). 'Bleed for me.'
29.name: Jason's Blood essence abilities (full progression)

30.content: Sin [Recovery]: Punish (special attack: necrotic + Sin; bronze Price of Absolution; silver Wages of Sin/Penance; gold Thief of Spirit). Castigate (spell: brand + Sin + Mark of Sin; bronze Weight of Sin + Marshal of Judgement; silver Mortality; gold Mark of Sin resists cleanse; 'Bear the mark of your transgressions'). Feast of Absolution (spell: iron removes curses/diseases/poisons/unholy from others; bronze Penance + Legacy of Sin per removal; silver wide area; gold allies gain Resistant + Integrity; 'Feed me your sins'). Sin Eater (special ability: iron resistance + Resistant; bronze Integrity; silver exceed baseline; gold consume allies' afflictions over time). Hegemony (aura: iron +ally/-enemy resistance; bronze Sin on attackers; silver transcendent damage downgraded; gold no splitting strength).
30.name: Jason's Sin essence abilities (full progression)

31.content: Doom [Spirit]: Inexorable Doom (spell: periodically reapply; bronze Inescapable; silver Persecution; gold accelerated; 'Your fate is to suffer'). Blade of Doom (conjuration: iron dagger Vulnerable; bronze Ruination of Spirit/Blood/Flesh; silver sword with Price in Blood (Ruin the Blade of Tribulation; Penitent the Blade of Sacrifice); gold extra damage per Legacy of Sin). Punition (spell: necrotic damage per affliction; bronze Penitence; silver mana tiers; gold area variant; 'Suffer the cost of your transgressions'). Verdict (execute spell: transcendent damage scaling with injury; bronze Penance; silver Sanction; gold wide-area ongoing; 'Mine is the judgement, and the judgement is death'). Avatar of Doom (familiar Gordon: iron one eye; bronze 4 orbs; silver Harbinger of Doom; gold butterflies create clouds and 12 orbs). Inevitable Demise (aura from the divine stone of Inevitability, refused). Awakened aura/other: Doom is his confluence.
31.name: Jason's Doom essence abilities (full progression)

32.content: Key effects from Jason's kit: Bleeding (absorbs healing), Leech Toxin, Tainted Meridians, Thief of Life/Spirit (drain), Necrotoxin, Blood From a Stone (negates blood/poison immunity), Exsanguination, Sin (increased necrotic damage), Wages of Sin, Price of Absolution, Penance (transcendent DoT), Penitence, Weight of Sin (transcendent damage when healed), Mark of Sin (tracking beacon; Marshal of Judgement), Mortality (negates curse immunity), Legacy of Sin (execute scaling), Creeping Death, Rigor Mortis, Weakness of the Flesh, Vulnerable, Ruination x3, Price in Blood, Inescapable (no teleport), Persecution (resist cleanse/heals), Sanction (reduced healing), Harbinger of Doom (butterflies spread afflictions), Sacrificial Victim; boons Blood Frenzy, Blood of the Immortal, Strength of My Enemies, Endless Power, Blood Glutton, Integrity, Resistant, Marshal of Judgement, Guardian's Blessing/Blessing's Bounty/Hegemon's Authority, Hegemon's Mercy/Benevolent Hegemon, Ghost Fire.
32.name: Boons and Afflictions list (Jason)

33.content: Titles: Godless Prophet (Book 2), Resolute (Book 3), Spirit Warrior (Book 3), Indomitable (Books 4 & 6), Giant Slayer (Book 5), Reality Hegemon (Book 6), Keeper of the Cycle (Book 10), 'the Hegemon' (public name after Boko), 'Rejector' / 'Defier' / 'Heretic King' (enemy names). Items: Hegemon's Will, Hegemon's Dominion, Amulet of the Dark Guardian, Cloud Flask, Night Fang, Trap Weaver Battle Robe, Dark Hydra Robe, Necklace of the Deep, Oasis Bracelet, Ritualist's Umbrella, Immortal Crest (soul crest), Genesis Command: Life/Source, Projection Command: Presence.
33.name: Jason's Titles and Items

34.content: Mirage chambers create illusions for training (dome with illusion bodies); the Mirage Chamber Association runs leagues in Jayapura (iron/bronze/silver divisions). Geller estate and Remore Academy annexes in Greenstone run training for iron-rankers; Remore Academy (Vitesse; chancellor Roland Remore; dean of ritual magic school; Belinda professor; Rufus Earth instructor) trains elite adventurers; Asano Academy on Earth (Emi, Clive, Belinda, Lorelei).
34.name: Mirage chambers and Training

35.comment: Essences and Races glossary: Smoulder and Brighthearts
35.content: Magical sub-species formed by centuries of exposure to elemental/array magic (Brightheart Smoulder; Moonstalker Elves; Thunder King Leonids; Sky Eater Elves; Blood Song Leonids) are inherently magical but no longer essence-users.
35.name: Essences and Races glossary: Smoulder and Brighthearts

37.comment: Current state of the story at the end of Book 13
37.content: State at the end of Book 13: Jason (gold prime avatar, ~39% to diamond; ~44) is trapped by Umber's ritual: his consciousness is bound to the prime avatar and his astral kingdom and domains' influence are sealed; he is being taken somewhere 'that isn't a universe'. Knowledge (celestine form, onyx hair) has an army at Ascension's Gate (former Sky Link island) and will cross the completed Earth-Pallimustus bridge to become the one true God of Earth; she ripped out Gabrielle's divine essence. Roland Remore and Victor Volaire's ~40 diamonds made a deal to stay out. Helsveth removed Team Biscuit (Humphrey, Sophie, Neil, Belinda, Clive, Rufus...) via the World-Phoenix; Stash hugged Jason; Clive absorbed Onslow into a tattoo. Earth: vampire war over (Gerling, McKean, Magdalyn dead; Elizabeth, Marie, Remy captured in Jason's vampire city). The Wild Thornberrys, EDJI, SESA and the clan are in place; Jason promised to kill Knowledge. Book 14 is announced as the final book.
37.name: Current state of the story at the end of Book 13

38.comment: Book 1 - Summary (Jason's arrival to Farrah's death)
38.content: BOOK 1 (Pallimustus, first ~4 months): Jason Asano, a ~23-year-old Australian retail middle manager, wakes naked and hairless in the hedge maze of Vane Estate (Vane Manor) on Pallimustus with a System-like interface (quests, inventory, character sheet) and a World-Phoenix Token. He kills Landemere Vane, absorbs Dark Essence, and frees/joins Rufus Remore, Gary (Gareth Xandier), Farrah Hurin and (briefly) Anisa Lasalle, captives of the Vane family Blood Cult (a Red Table branch). Together they kill the cult (Cressida Vane, Alicia, Darryl Caruthers) and a Sanguine Horror; Jason gains Blood, Sin and Doom essences (Doom is the confluence of Dark+Blood+Sin) and reaches Iron rank. Anisa is fired after killing a traitor contact and trying to kill Colin. Jason goes to Greenstone, meets Danielle and Humphrey Geller, Gabrielle Pellin, Clive Standish, Jory Tillman, Sophie Wexler and Belinda Callahan, learns the Way of the Reaper, passes the Adventure Society field assessment and rises to three stars. He clashes with Thadwick Mercer, crime lords Ventress/Silva/Dorgan and Magic Society director Lucian Lamprey, and sees the Healer and Dominion judge the Church of the Healer. In an astral-space expedition against automaton masters, Farrah Hurin is killed (month 4) and Henry Geller dies; Emir Bahadir arrives to help. The book ends with the expedition aftermath, the trek to Boko and Rufus's grief.
38.name: Book 1 - Summary (Jason's arrival to Farrah's death)

39.content: Jason Asano (born on Earth, Australia; ~23 at arrival, 44 by Book 12). Former middle manager at an office-supply/retail business who dropped out of political science and lived in Melbourne; irreverent, rambling, pop-culture-quoting joker with a strong moral core, self-doubt and a habit of acting the villain. Arrives on Pallimustus bald with no body hair, speaking all languages via Mysterious Stranger. Mixed Japanese-Australian: father Ken Asano (Japan-born landscape architect), mother Cheryl (Japan-obsessed), older sister Erika (daughter Emi), brother Kaito (Mum's favoured son; married Jason's ex-girlfriend). Four essences absorbed in Book 1: Dark (Speed), Blood (Power), Sin (Recovery), Doom confluence (Spirit) - an 'affliction specialist' build. Early abilities: Midnight Eyes, Cloak of Night, Path of Shadows, Blood Harvest, Leech Bite, Feast of Blood, Sanguine Horror (Colin), Punish, Feast of Absolution, Sin Eater, Hegemony, Inexorable Doom, Punition, Blade of Doom, Verdict, Castigate, Haemorrhage. Fights with the Way of the Reaper martial art, Dread Salvation sword (from Gary), Night Fang dagger and a Trap Weaver Battle Robe. Immune to tracking/identification. See later entries for his growth: Bronze, Silver, the Hegemon, Prime Avatar and System Administrator.
39.name: Jason Asano

40.content: Rufus Remore: tall, bald, handsome Black man from Vitesse (voice 'like dark chocolate'), grandson of diamond-ranker Roland Remore (chancellor of Remore Academy); father Gabriel Remore, mother Arabelle. Leader/guide of Jason's first adventuring group, fencer-type (scimitar of golden light, silver swords, water-walking boots, speed/time-freeze ability). Moral anchor: told Jason on his first night what an adventurer is - someone who stands between the bad things and those who need protecting; rule 'personal possessions only' when looting. Guilt-stricken after Farrah dies ('she followed me'). Childhood friend of the Crown Princess of Vitesse; in a relationship with Vincent Trenslow (Book 1). Mentor-like friend of Emir Bahadir. Later a major gold-rank force on Earth beside Taika.
40.name: Rufus Remore

41.content: Gareth 'Gary' Xandier: huge leonid (lion-headed, growly) crafter-warrior with forge/iron powers: conjured dark runed steel armour, hammer and shield, a foundry golem summon (from iron filings). Rufus's friend; deeply loyal and practical; makes Jason's sword Dread Salvation ('first and last gift'). Dominion notes him ('Gareth Xandier... that is where monarchs come from'). In Book 10 he drinks the Cup of Heroes and becomes a demigod; in Book 11 he refuses a natural-array alternative, dies ~1 year later and is reincarnated as a baby leonid; by Book 12 he is a teenage leonid, 'Gary Sharpton'. Jason calls him 'brother'.
41.name: Gary (Gareth Xandier) - original

42.content: Farrah Hurin: small, pale, strawberry-blonde with a button nose and a savage, wise temperament; Vitesse-born ritual magician and Magic Society member (parents Amelia and William Hurin). Essences Earth, Fire, Potent -> Volcano confluence: Lava Cannon, Magma Golem (obsidian powder), Flamecore Ravager, Magma Trap, Volcanic Resurgence. Teaches Jason aura control, perception, meditation and ritual circles (taught the summoning circle for Colin). DIES in Book 1 (month 4, automaton ambush: four metal arms of a silver abomination pierce body and head); funeral month 5. Revived and found on Earth in Book 4 (as a second outworlder), reaches silver and gold; in Book 12 chooses to become an immortal Defier of the Will. Confidante of Jason; co-founder with Travis Noble of the Sky Link Company.
42.name: Farrah Hurin

43.content: Anisa Lasalle: platinum-blonde elf, healer-priestess of Purity (her church wanted the Vane estate), spell Regenerate ('Let the life that has withered return to full bloom'). Initially on Rufus's team; kills the traitor contact in a desert cabin before he can talk and tries to kill Colin as 'tainted'. Rufus fires her; she takes the wagon and animals and calls humans 'filth'. Cassandra Mercer later learns she belongs to the Lasalle family.
43.name: Anisa Lasalle

44.comment: Vane Family (Blood Cult) and Vane Estate
44.content: Vane Estate/Vane Manor: lush estate in a Kalahari-like region (two moons overhead) with climate-pillar magic, hedge maze, well and subterranean ritual chamber; seat of a Blood Cult branch of the Red Table. Lady Cressida Vane (matriarch), son Landemere Vane (Builder cultist, astral specialist; tried to summon an astral being and pulled Jason across; killed by Jason's Seal Knife; familiar Umbral Mountain Snake), daughter Alicia Vane (killed by Gary's trowel), Cressida's husband Darryl Caruthers (high priest), and servant Dougall (cannibal with shovel). They were building a Sanguine Horror. Jason kills most of them; Cressida and Darryl die after he shoves them into stone. The Adventure Society later names a conference room the 'Edith Vane Memorial'.
44.name: Vane Family (Blood Cult) and Vane Estate

45.content: Sanguine Horror: an apocalypse beast of carrion/lamprey leeches in blood-soaked bandages; regenerates from a single leech; weak to salt and lava (weaknesses fade by gold rank). Jason's Awakening Stone of the Apocalypse gives the Sanguine Horror familiar ability; he names it COLIN ('Team Colin'): a leech on his shoulder that communicates left=yes/right=no, melts into blood to heal him, swarm form, 'worm-that-walks' form (bronze), blood robes (silver), gold: can exceed mass limits via life drain. Summoned familiars can vanish into the summoner and die with them; bonded familiars survive their owner but cannot vanish. At diamond Colin reaches full sanguine-horror strength.
45.name: Sanguine Horror / Colin

46.content: Greenstone: coastal city on the Mistrun River delta in a low-magic desert region (exports green marble and lesser spirit coins). Split into the Old City (red-yellow 12m walls, harbour) and The Island (rich district/breakwater of green marble reached by four bridges with a permit system). Magic trams run through water tunnels. Divine Square holds temples of Dominion, Journey/Roads, Knowledge, Healer. Fortress (neutral crime-lord ground with pit fights), Cavendish district, Broadstreet Clinic (Jory), Sailor's Watch inn (Madam Landry/Jessica), Adventure Society hall and trade hall, Magic Society (Lucian Lamprey, Clive), Geller estate. Nominally ruled by the Duke of Greenstone. Monster surge every ~10 years. Later hosts the Geller-Remore training facility.
46.name: Greenstone

47.content: The Gellers: a large, tough, honour-bound adventuring clan (broad shoulders, chiselled features) from Greenstone who deliberately train in low-magic conditions. Members include Danielle (matriarch/strategist), Humphrey, Rick, Phoebe, Jonah, Henry (died Book 1), Henrietta, Valdis. Operate the Geller-Seven spirit coin farm; a diamond-rank ancestor is rumoured. Later partner with Remore Academy (Geller-Remore facility).
47.name: Geller Family

48.content: Danielle Geller: looks ~30, actually ~50, silver-ranker (time-confluence essence; dimensional blade, acceleration, damage reflection) and Humphrey's mother; diplomat/strategist who becomes Jason's adviser on etiquette and politics (hired as political advisor in Book 12). Investigated Jason for Gabriel Remore; fought in the ambush where Farrah died.
48.name: Danielle Geller

49.content: Humphrey Geller: tall, broad, handsome Geller who becomes leader of Jason's team (Team Biscuit). Dragon-confluence essence: dragon wings, rainbow-scale armour, dragon-wing sword and angel-feather sword, fire breath, Spartoi dragon-tooth warriors, Dragon Might aura, Dive Bomb, Unstoppable Force, later Mighty Strength and Immortality; familiar Stash (Velitraxistaasch, shapeshifting dragon: puppy/canary/hill mouse/rainbow dragon). Failed Rufus's field assessment first (boldness); Hero's Drive racial gift. Early romance with Gabrielle Pellin. Likes Jason's biscuits. In Book 1 confronts Jason over mirage-arena cruelty.
49.name: Humphrey Geller

50.content: Gabrielle Pellin: acolyte, later priestess, of Knowledge; blue-and-white robes, might essence, conjured iron staff. Initially disapproves of Jason ('dangerous ideas'); her goddess takes interest in him. Humphrey's early girlfriend; later married to Travis Noble. Jason apologises to her in Book 12.
50.name: Gabrielle Pellin

51.content: Sophie Wexler 'the Nightingale': celestine woman (chocolate skin, silver hair and eyes). Arrived as a toddler with her father (muscle for a merchant group); he worked for Silva; after his failed expedition she was indentured with huge debt and fought in Fortress pits, then became a thief with Belinda Callahan. Speed essence (wall/water running, later Eternal Moment time acceleration). Sheltered by Clarissa Ventress, hunted by Cole Silva and Lucian Lamprey. Jason claims her via the right of first refusal (Book 1-2) and she joins his team. Fights in her father's Way-of-the-Reaper style. Later she and Humphrey become a couple (engaged by Book 11). Her indentured past drives her fierce support of Jason's anti-slavery System shutdown in Book 12.
51.name: Sophie Wexler

52.content: Belinda 'Lindy' Callahan: short scraggly-haired human, Sophie's friend, planner and tool-maker thief turned adventurer. Later powers: Instant Adept (temporary roles via item sets), Force Tether, Mirror Magic (copies and double-casts Farrah's/Clive's spells), scout/tracker. Courted by Jory Tillman. Team Biscuit's tactician and gadgeteer; helps abduct Cyrion nobles in Book 12.
52.name: Belinda Callahan

53.content: Clive Standish: tall lanky scholar from an eel farm, Magic Society researcher with rune-based essences (circles, Rune Trap, Mantle of Retribution, Wrath of the Magister, Mana Equilibrium). Familiar Onslow, a rune tortoise (flying battle platform later). Venerates the Celestial Book. Astral-magic expert; explains the cosmos to Jason as 'dumpling soup'. Becomes founder/Archchancellor of the Magic Research Association (Book 12) and co-inventor of the sky link. Unmarried: the 'imaginary wife' is a running gag in the series; by Book 13 his partner is Lorelei Grantham.
53.name: Clive Standish

54.content: Jory Tillman: iron-rank alchemist-adventurer with the Broadstreet Clinic in Greenstone Old City; sells cheap potions, crystal wash and 'Togetherness Jelly'. Jason invests 3 gold coins in him. Smitten with Belinda. By Book 12 a leading alchemist who travels to Earth. The Church of the Healer once branded him heretic; the Healer blesses his clinic.
54.name: Jory Tillman

55.content: Neil Davone: healer-adventurer who stands with Jory against the Healer's priests; joins the Church of the Healer's penitents and becomes a priest of the Healer; later Team Biscuit's body healer (Grand Renewal, summons, buffs). Serves Thadwick Mercer in Book 1 before quitting. Jason's friend/foil; Cassandra Mercer's ex.
55.name: Neil Davone

56.content: Mercer family of Greenstone Island: Lady Thalia Mercer (silver adventurer-turned-noble, wants Cassandra to wed Rufus), husband Beaufort Mercer, son Thadwick Mercer (storm/lightning-potent essences; incompetent, cheats the assessment system, land-grab scheme with summoned fergax; flees the ambush leaving allies) and daughter Cassandra Mercer (olive skin, dark hair, hidden aura; clever; one-night stand with Jason; later Neil's ex; reaches silver). Thalia is the Duke of Greenstone's sister-in-law.
56.name: Mercer Family (Thalia, Thadwick, Cassandra)

57.comment: Elspeth Arella and Adventure Society Greenstone
57.content: Elspeth Arella: elf, silver, Director of the Greenstone Adventure Society branch; rose from poverty; daughter of crime lord Adris Dorgan (hidden); scheming but reformist; aims to oust Lucian Lamprey; promotes Jason to 3 stars. Staff: Vincent Trenslow (waxed twirled moustache, strict instructor, Rufus's partner), Genevieve Picot (deputy director), Guy Spalding (corrupt official tied to Silva), Albert Bertinelli (clerk; one of the 'Berts' octuplets: Bertram, Herbert, Robert, Gilbert, Filbert, Hubert, Bertrand).
57.name: Elspeth Arella and Adventure Society Greenstone

58.comment: Greenstone Crime Lords (Big Three) and Fortress
58.content: Big Three of Greenstone's underworld: Clarissa Ventress (ambitious, canal-district mansion; shelters Sophie as bait against Silva), Cole Silva (impetuous, obsessed with Sophie) and Adris Dorgan (elf, bronze, 'the quiet one', Elspeth Arella's father). The Fortress is an ancient warehouse-district stone arena/neutral ground. Lucian Lamprey (muscular elf, Magic Society Greenstone director, banished there) rents a box and is obsessed with the Nightingale; his deputy Pochard Finn is Clive's boss.
58.name: Greenstone Crime Lords (Big Three) and Fortress

59.content: Way of the Reaper: legendary iron skill book found by Rufus's team under a lake (two crossed scythes over a skull). Five forms: Sage (mobile, vs many/limbed enemies), Hierophant (direct, aggressive), Trickster (drunken-boxing style), Hunter (debilitating attacks on the unaware, find weak points), Hermit (counters/defence vs humans and bizarre monsters). Key skill is transitions between forms. Jason learns it in Book 1; Clive finds copies in an ancient Order of the Reaper complex under Greenstone (Forms One and Three). Sophie's father also used it. Emir Bahadir investigates the Order of the Reaper (ancient assassin order).
59.name: Way of the Reaper (martial art)

60.content: Dread Salvation: iron legendary growth sword made by Gary for Jason (red-gold hilt, black tassel). Stacking buffs Stone Cutter (vs physical immunity) and Spell Breaker (vs magical immunity) built from resonating-force damage when immunities trigger. Growth upgrades need huge rare materials. Jason keeps it for life; called 'the first and last gift from Gary' (Book 12).
60.name: Dread Salvation

61.comment: The Healer, Dominion and Knowledge (Book 1 divine events)
61.content: Healer's Judgement (Greenstone): when the Chief Priest of the Healer marches on Jory's Broadstreet Clinic, the god Healer appears (small, middle-aged, plain brown robes), regrows a foot, strips corrupt clergy of their essences and welcomes Neil; Dominion (young, handsome, crowned, cruel-eyed, fire aura) offers to take the stripped power-seekers; the Healer seals the penitents' returned essences and blesses the clinic. Knowledge (Mediterranean-looking woman) meets Jason in her temple: he was not chosen, the World-Phoenix Token is his way home and will use itself 'when circumstances dictate'. Dominion says of Jason 'I love that guy'.
61.name: The Healer, Dominion and Knowledge (Book 1 divine events)

62.content: Book 1 climax: Danielle Geller leads a large Greenstone expedition into the desert astral space (turquoise lagoon, 5-sided engraved columns relaying astral magic) after Ustei nomads flee north. A construct army (wooden puppets, stone golems, clockwork animals, steel spider) led by sandy-robed bronze/silver masters and silver-rank abominations (metal grafted into flesh, four extra metal arms) ambushes them. Farrah Hurin is killed; Henry Geller dies; Jonah and Thadwick+3 are found injured; Rufus loses an arm and is crushed by guilt. Emir's cloud palace and portaler Hester (via Boko) help; two captives suicide by exploding crystals. The network of astral nodes is disrupted. Boko is a dark-skinned human desert city and the mainland base.
62.name: Automaton Ambush (Desert Astral Space)

63.content: Emir Bahadir: gold-ranker, midnight-black skin and beaded hair, Rufus's mentor-ally; wealthy Vitesse-based finder of rare items for diamond/gold clients; owns a dimensional-jacket flask holding cloud forms (estate, bus, palace, ship) and a 300m x 60m cloud ship. Wife Constance (silver, pale, brown hair; indispensable). Staff include portaler Hester. In Book 12 supports Jason in Cyrion. Ketis Bahadir is a relative.
63.name: Emir Bahadir and Constance

64.comment: Mirage Chamber, Skill Books and Spirit Coins
64.content: Mirage chamber: dome with illusion bodies for safe training (limited by local magic). Skill books impart techniques via a text swarm and must be absorbed while conscious. Spirit coin ladder: 100 lesser = 1 iron; then x10 each: iron -> bronze -> silver -> gold -> diamond (gold coin = 100,000 lesser). Consuming a higher-rank coin temporarily raises attributes to that rank with backlash. Lesser coins are Greenstone's biggest export. Jason's coins carry his thumbs-up face ('PRODUCT OF JASON / G'DAY MATE').
64.name: Mirage Chamber, Skill Books and Spirit Coins

65.comment: Book 2 - Summary (Sky Scar Lake and the Legacy of the Reaper)
65.content: BOOK 2: Jason confronts Elspeth Arella, wins Sophie's six-month indenture at a hearing and makes her an adventurer (Swift, Balance, Wind -> Mystic confluence; Iron rank). Belinda joins as Clive's research assistant, later Charlatan confluence (Magic, Trap, Adept). A Continental Council inquiry (Tabitha Gert) demotes Jason to one star and Danielle/Humphrey to two. Star-seed Builder cultists are exposed: Jonah Geller dies when the Purity archbishop tries to purge a star seed; Thadwick's seed is extracted; Timos, a Builder cultist, recruits Thadwick. Jason forms a team with Humphrey, Clive, Sophie and Neil Davone (Prosperity confluence). Emir Bahadir stages a contest for the Scythe of the Reaper in the Order of the Reaper's hidden astral space under Sky Scar Lake: the City of Fallen Echoes with five Legacy trials (courage, intellect, resolve, capability, wisdom) and a hidden sixth insight trial. Jason takes the real Scythe, gets the Reaper Token and Shade (Shadow of the Reaper familiar) and Gordon (Avatar of Doom). Teammates' racial gifts transfigure. Cole Silva schemes. Jason meets Zara Rimaros. Jason receives the Godless Prophet title. Emir gives the team a Cloud Palace; Jason binds a Cloud Flask and houseboat. The book ends with a raid on a Builder island camp where Rufus unleashes Kingdom of Eclipse; Timos and Thadwick escape.
65.name: Book 2 - Summary (Sky Scar Lake and the Legacy of the Reaper)

66.comment: Tabitha Gert and the Continental Council Inquiry
66.content: Tabitha Gert: strict rule-following Adventure Society official (black pin) who leads the Continental Council inquiry into the Greenstone expedition disaster. Demotes Jason to one star (Cassandra Mercer then breaks off their relationship, 'We end here'), demotes Danielle and Humphrey to two stars, expels the Phael family from the Society, and serves as interim Greenstone director. Believes rules are the basis of civilisation.
66.name: Tabitha Gert and the Continental Council Inquiry

67.comment: Star Seeds and the Builder's Plan
67.content: Star seeds: hair-thin metal-wire implants (nucleus like a hulled coconut) made by great astral beings (here the Builder) that puppet the host, transform them into flesh-steel abominations and explode into crystal if the host talks. The Builder wants to sever astral spaces from the world and hold them intact to build its own world (cataclysmic for the planet). Timos is a long-embedded cultist in Greenstone (kills Frank the tunnel worker). Five star-seed hosts (Jonah Geller, Thadwick Mercer and three others) were used as decoys; Jonah dies in a Purity purge, Thadwick survives extraction. Builder cultists summoned Jason by accident while trying to summon a Clockwork King. The Church of Purity quietly tolerates the cult via a wider accord, and Archbishop Nicolas Hendren/Herston is complicit.
67.name: Star Seeds and the Builder's Plan

68.content: The Builder (original): a great astral being obsessed with physical reality it cannot share; builds its own world out of stolen astral spaces; recruits cults with gifts of power, uses star seeds and constructs (golems, clockwork animals). Native gold-rank Clockwork Kings of the Builder's world are dragon-like leaders. The Builder's cult attacked Cyrion in the past (world engineer golems left outside the walls). In Book 3 Jason confronts and sanctions it; the Builder's role passes to a messenger (the new Builder). See Book 3 for details.
68.name: The Builder (original)

69.content: Order of the Reaper: ancient royal assassins (knife in the dark for mad rulers) and hunters of undead/necromancers, accepted by nations and churches until the church of the Unliving and Purity, in an unholy compact, destroyed it. Churches also bargained with vorger (deep-astral entities) to turn fleeing initiates into flesh abominations. The last grandmaster (an outworlder with dark essence) hid survivors and the Legacy of the Reaper in a proto-astral space (the City of Fallen Echoes) under Sky Scar Lake, with trials open 18 days and iron-rank entry only. The hidden insight trial reveals the Order survives as a quiet volunteer network matching tasks to people of conscience; the trials are recruitment bait. The real Scythe of the Reaper (silver blade, gold shaft, obsidian inlay; diamond-rank, enormously heavy) is delivered to Emir Bahadir by Jason. The Way of the Reaper martial art comes from the Order.
69.name: Order of the Reaper

70.content: City of Fallen Echoes: ancient circular overgrown city in an astral space (12 gate towers; sea around) entered through Sky Scar Lake's drowned fortress. Trials: choose wisdom or courage first (wisdom gives Medallion of Escape + Lesser Miracle Potion); city traversal (capability); nightmare-hag courage test (Jason faces an evil future self; Humphrey his family); intellect constellation puzzle (reward Summoner's Die: Form); resolve (refuse to execute captive priests; reward Immortal Crest); hidden insight trial. Monsters: siege golems, margolls, sloth demon, grizzards, vorger swarms, flesh abominations, blood root vine (killed by Jason, Jory, Beth and others). 19 adventurers pass all trials; ~419 time-displaced priests and holy warriors are freed. The astral space is at gold monster density mostly iron, some bronze.
70.name: City of Fallen Echoes

71.content: Shade: British-sounding living silhouette, invigilator of the Legacy trials and a fragment of the Reaper's shadow (also familiar of the grandmaster); becomes Jason's Dark familiar via the Awakening Stone of the Reaper ('Shadow of the Reaper', later Shadow of the Hegemon). Incorporeal, up to three bodies (later 211), hides in other people's shadows, drains mana by touch, lets Jason see through bodies. Polite, dry, indispensable; pilots Jason's ships and acts as butler. 'The laws of physics are strong suggestions.' In Book 11 Shade sanctions himself becoming the Shadow of the Hegemon.
71.name: Shade (Shadow of the Reaper)

72.content: Gordon: Jason's Doom familiar (Avatar of Doom). Appears as a nebula eye (orange eye, blue iris) in a dark cloak with two orbiting eye-orbs (blue-in-orange, orange-in-blue); communicates yes/no by orbs; orange orb fires resonating-force, blue orb disruptive-force beams; afflicts Vulnerable; can subsume into Jason's aura to mask or strengthen it. Chant: 'When worlds end, you are the arbiter... I have doom to bring.' At gold: butterflies create affliction clouds; Harbinger of Doom spreads afflictions.
72.name: Gordon (Avatar of Doom)

73.comment: Reaper Token and Racial Gift Transfiguration
73.content: Astral blessing tokens (like Jason's Reaper Token) trigger racial-gift evolution. After the Legacy contest: Jason's Map -> Tactical Map; Clive's Human Ambition -> Thirst for Knowledge; Neil's Life Affinity -> Life Guard; Sophie's Mana Integrity -> Mana Wellspring; Humphrey's Special Attack Affinity -> Attack of the Mirage Dragon (illusory double of special attacks); Stash is revealed as a rare Mirage Dragon. Jason's Mysterious Stranger became Dark Rider. Gifts are tailored to the soul. Awakening Stone of the Reaper (unranked legendary, one per adventurer who reached the tower) awakens Reaper-themed abilities: Jason Shadow of the Reaper, Hand of the Reaper and Avatar of Doom; Neil Hero's Moment and Reaper's Redoubt; Humphrey Spirit Reaper and Immortality; Sophie Deny the Reaper.
73.name: Reaper Token and Racial Gift Transfiguration

74.content: After Jason frees the time-displaced priests and holy warriors, the Healer, Dominion and other gods appear in the priest camp to thank him; the pressure alters his aura and grants the title Godless Prophet (aura gains an echo of transcendent power). Stash, shapeshifted as Jason, caused a streaking incident.
74.name: Godless Prophet (title) and Gods' thanks

75.content: Zara Rimaros: celestine princess (caramel skin, sapphire eyes, waterfall-blue Rimaros royal-line hair) of the Storm Kingdom (Rimaros), former 'Hurricane Princess'. Meets Jason when he teleports into her tent (he offers gem-berry and milk-nut squares); gives only 'Zara'. Aunt Vesper Rimaros. Disgraced by a series of mistakes, she adventured as Zara Nareen with Orin's team then Jason's; storm/wind area attacks later concentrated into fist-sized storms. Romantic tension with Jason grows (Book 12: she restores her sapphire hair, resumes her princess role, wants the Storm Kingdom to abolish indenture). In Book 2 she is iron-rank. See Rimaros entries.
75.name: Zara Rimaros (Hurricane Princess)

76.content: Valdis Volaire: slight blond prince of the Kingdom of Mirrors (ruled eight centuries by the diamond-ranker the Mirror King, Victor Volaire; Valdis is son of the queen consort). Essences sword, swift, adept, master; dimensional jacket, expensive gear; dueling-obsessed. Joins Clive's team in Fallen Echoes. Challenges everyone aboard Jason's ship to duels in Book 12.
76.name: Valdis Volaire

77.content: Neil Davone: elf (chubby for an elf, muscular under clothes) of the Davone family of Greenstone's Island. Essences shield, growth, renewal -> Prosperity confluence: healing, cleansing, Burst Shield, Absorbing Shield, buffs (Giant's Might, Armour of Renewal), Fountain of Life, Bolster, Reels of Fortune (random effects), Spoils of Victory (aura), Chrysalis Golem summon, Hero's Moment, Reaper's Redoubt, Life Guard. Joins Jason after Jason invites him ('honest foot forward'). Crushed on Cassandra Mercer.
77.name: Neil Davone (Prosperity)

78.content: Team formed late Book 2: Jason (dark/blood/sin/doom), Humphrey (might, magic, wing, dragon), Clive (magic, rune, balance, karmic), Sophie (swift, wind, balance, mystic), Neil (shield, growth, renewal, prosperity), later Belinda (magic, trap, adept, charlatan), Zara and others. Tactic: buff Humphrey with Clive and Neil and let him go; Clive and Neil act as bait. Jason's biscuits give the team its name. Beth Cavendish's and Rick Geller's teams are rivals in the mirage chamber.
78.name: Humphrey's Team / Early Team Biscuit

79.content: Sophie's 20 abilities (Swift/Balance/Wind/Mystic): Free Runner, Avatar of Speed, Between the Raindrops, Alacrity's Reward, Eternal Moment (Swift); Equilibrium, Cloud Step, Moment of Oneness, Karmic Warrior, Deny the Reaper (Balance); Wind Blade, Cleansing Breeze (aura), Leaf on the Wind, Wind Wave, Child of the Celestial Wind (Wind); Strong Soul, Sight Beyond Sight, Immortal Fist, Radiant Fist, Mirage Step (Mystic). Racial gift Mana Wellspring. Wields Siege Grips; unarmed 'empty hand' skill better than Rufus's.
79.name: Sophie Wexler's Abilities

80.content: Belinda's essences: Magic (Bag of Tricks, Power Thief, spell mimicry, Astral Lantern), Trap (Bait and Switch, rune trap, pit trap, tethers/Force Tether), Adept (Blessing of Readiness, cooldown aura, Instant Adept), Charlatan confluence (Echo Spirit, Beside Myself, Unexpected Allies, Counterfeit Combatant, Specious Sorcerer). Familiars: Shimmer (astral lantern: disruptive bolts, negates projectiles) and Gemini (echo spirit: mimics forms, switch-teleport). Gifts: Adventurer's Tools, Quick Learner, The Price of Power, Face in the Crowd, Form and Function.
80.name: Belinda Callahan's Abilities

81.comment: Jason's Cloud Palace, Cloud Flask and Houseboat
81.content: Emir awards the winning team a bonded Cloud Palace (a growth item; Jason chosen as bonded owner); Jason binds a Cloud Flask (iron legendary growth item, soul-bound; adaptive; grows with bronze air/water and dimension quintessence) and summons an adaptive three-storey houseboat at Marina North, Greenstone. Over time it becomes his huge cloud ship (cruise-ship size, can shift into configurations like D20 icosahedron with eye-panels, a floating cloud palace, a passenger ship, a temple of Jason).
81.name: Jason's Cloud Palace, Cloud Flask and Houseboat

82.content: Soul crest: tattoo on the soul showing on the body; unique permanent ID verified worldwide by the Adventure Society; form reflects true nature. Tilly (old, wiry, no aura; knew young Emir, Gabriel and Arabelle) applies them in Jayapura. Jason's crest: a dark empty cloak under a silver-starred night with an open blue sky and golden sun at chest, 'the day hidden in the night'. Magical tattoos last until next rank (iron tattoos: burst recovery, DR burst, cooldown reduction, affliction-resistance reduction for Jason).
82.name: Immortal Crest (Soul Crest) and Tilly

83.content: Rufus's extra powers: golden sun sword leaves burning sun orbs; silver moon sword leaves chilling moons; after-image chain teleports; speed of light; ultimate Kingdom of Eclipse (chant 'Darkness and light, sun and moon...') firing an eclipse orb transcendent beam. At the end of Book 2 he uses it on the silver-rank abomination that killed Farrah in the Builder island raid, killing dozens but not it, and collapses.
83.name: Rufus Remore - Kingdom of Eclipse

84.comment: Mirror King and Kingdom of Mirrors
84.content: Mirror King (Victor Volaire): diamond-ranker ruling a small rich Kingdom of Mirrors for ~800 years; father of Valdis. Friend and ally of Roland Remore; rules via mirror domain. Mentioned again Book 12 as having tea with Roland.
84.name: Mirror King and Kingdom of Mirrors

85.content: After Sophie slips beyond reach, Cole Silva kills a thug and hires Killian Laurent (sickly elf with 'particular appetites') to find a silver-rank adventurer who will quietly take Sophie and kill Jason; someone offers hidden help. The Builder cult's Timos recruits Thadwick Mercer (now a puppet-in-waiting).
85.name: Cole Silva schemes (Killian Laurent)

86.content: Hester Maharala: silver portal-user of Emir's staff, from Jayapura (large northern port of Pranay, a Sri Lanka-like landmass; world lacks Arabia so the Mediterranean joins the Indian Ocean). Mother Anise; family lifted by essences/cores. Jayapura has float discs, glowing-frame airships, Mystic Quarter, and the Mirage Chamber Association leagues for iron/bronze/silver (no gold division; pros avoid cores near silver). She can portal to places she has visited; closest to the desert aperture is the city Boko.
86.name: Hester Maharala

87.content: Lesser Miracle Potion: iron legendary alchemy that fully restores health/mana/stamina for normal/iron users. Jory finds its formula in the astral space and drinks mixed potions to become a patchwork super-strong 'Alchemical Abomination'; second form skinny and oily, dissolving vorger. His powers: Eldritch Eyes (orbs deliver potions), Potion Mystic, Universal Reagent.
87.name: Jory's Alchemical Abomination form

88.content: Jason grew up in a coastal tourist town (Casselton Beach) attending Casselton Educational Institute; mother in property sales, father a landscape architect; Japanese-heritage family. Older brother Kaito (socially chameleonic) and childhood sweetheart Amy (next door) later married, 'blew up my whole life'. He later worked assistant manager at a bulk office supplier ('Station-Eyrie' joke). Learned people fill gaps in stories. Gave worst-things quip about the town.
88.name: Jason's Backstory (told to Cassandra)

89.content: Beaufort Mercer facilitated the Builder cult's escape through Hornis; Thalia (might, potent, swift, onslaught; silver) tipped Danielle. A clay-and-iron doppelganger 'Thadwick' appears at the Mercer manor with star-seed-controlled guards before the cult retakes him; Timos kills Frank.
89.name: Mercer scandal and Thadwick's capture

90.content: Emir's old team: Emir, Gabriel Remore (gold; wind/fire sword dancer, dark curly hair), Arabelle Remore (Rufus's mother; rainbow-dyed hair; withering touch, urns of life force, healer), Callum 'Cal' Morse (gold stealth assassin, grizzled hunter). Ketis Bahadir is Emir's granddaughter (15, rainbow braids; learns the Way of the Reaper; her father died in the last monster surge). Amelia and William Hurin are Farrah's parents (bronze after Farrah's help). Staff nicknamed by shared first names ('Greg').
90.name: Emir's Staff and Associates

91.comment: Awakening Stones - Reaper, Celestials, Karma and others
91.content: Notable stones: Reaper (unranked legendary, 5 legendary stones awarded in Book 2), Celestials (created from an outworlder's ability; only 3 existed), Karma, Rebirth, Avatar, Rain (Sophie: Between the Raindrops), Moment (Sophie: Eternal Moment, Moment of Oneness), Preparation, Surge, Purgation (Cleansing Breeze), Sky (Leaf on the Wind). Divine stones (Inevitability, Persistence) from gods are revocable; astral-being gift stones are not. Jason refused Knowledge's 'poison pill' gifts: Divine Awakening Stone of Inevitability (aura Inevitable Demise), Soul-Purgation Tablet, Divine Awakening Stone of Persistence (spell Curse of Isolation).
91.name: Awakening Stones - Reaper, Celestials, Karma and others

92.comment: Book 3 - Summary (Star seed, Bronze rank, the Builder's boarding vessel, Jason's death)
92.content: BOOK 3: Winter-spring after the Reaper trials. Knowledge gifts Jason dimensional-transgression knowledge; Tabitha Gert and Arella restore his 3 stars after a road-contract punishment detail. Valkyrie mirage match: Jason's team beats Valdis's. Henrietta Geller supervises the road contract; Oasis Tyrant (silver elemental) at North East Quarry Village Four nearly kills Jason (soul scar, Amulet of the Dark Guardian, title Resolute). Clarissa Ventress dies; Cole Silva, Killian Laurent and Lucian Lamprey kidnap Jason (Mr Sparrow/Lawrence); Killian implants a Builder star seed that Jason expels in soul-space defiance (title Spirit Warrior; Defiant quest system; Colin rendered dormant then resummoned at bronze). Silva and Lamprey get skeletal suppression. Veldt bandit contract; Path of Shadows reaches bronze. Sophie's indenture ends. The anti-Builder council uses Jason as a 'star-seed detector' (the Rejector). The team enters the Order of the Reaper's astral space again, where the Builder cult (Zato, Timos, Dougall, Thadwick, Anisa, Archbishop Hendren of Purity) is building a tunnel; the team reaches bronze, kills Anisa (Humphrey), Hendren (Jason) and Zato; discovers the astral space is the Builder's boarding vessel; Clive's inversion device burns out the world engineers. The Builder (in Thadwick's body) collars Jason; Jason dies tackling it from the central tower. The World-Phoenix Token is consumed; Jason's body turns to rainbow smoke and he returns to Earth. In Interstice, the World-Phoenix, Reaper and Builder strike a deal: no more resurrection for Jason; the Builder may not interfere with Earth; Jason will get a trusted outworlder companion. Epilogues: Jason's disappearance investigated on Earth (Erika, DS Adam Cosgrove); Thalia Mercer meets the energy-vampire remnant of Thadwick; team splits; Dawn and Helsveth in Fueros.
92.name: Book 3 - Summary (Star seed, Bronze rank, the Builder's boarding vessel, Jason's death)

93.comment: Oasis Tyrant and Jason's soul scar
93.content: At North East Quarry Village Four a silver-rank water/earth elemental, the Oasis Tyrant (armoured woman of water and rock, razor-stone whip), manifests while Jason's team is away. Jason kites it alone with Shade and Gordon, loses Shade's bodies and Gordon, drinks a Lesser Miracle Potion and survives; gains the Amulet of the Dark Guardian (iron growth legendary: each affliction becomes a Guardian's Blessing absorb shield) and title Resolute (resist suppressive higher-rank auras). Henrietta Geller kills the tyrant. Jason is unconscious four days with a soul scar from hip to torso. Two elderly villagers died.
93.name: Oasis Tyrant and Jason's soul scar

94.content: Henrietta Geller: Humphrey's older sister (21 in Book 3), bronze summoning specialist with purple eyes (summoned familiar), a bonded desert phoenix, floating-eye, healing-lantern and other familiars; summons include a golden fire crow, winged centaur, four-winged angel, furnace golem; draws circles in the air; uses origami heidels. Supervises Jason's road contract; later silver and a rival friend of Cassandra Mercer. In Book 12 she is on Cassandra's team. Fire essence user (Fire Bolt). Father Keith Geller.
94.name: Henrietta Geller

95.content: Cole Silva, Killian Laurent (sickly elf; bone conjuration, skeletal arms; secretly Builder-linked) and Lucian Lamprey hire silver-ranker 'Mr Sparrow' (Lawrence; shadow-teleports; wears masks; Lamprey knows his sister) to abduct Jason with suppression collars. Jason is held at an abandoned Magic Society spirit-coin way station guarded by Remi, Coburn and Jerrick. Killian uses a Purity-seized star seed in a ritual to try to enslave Jason; Colin fights it from inside; Jason defies the Builder's will in his soul-space until the seed overloads and is expelled (title Spirit Warrior). Killian murders Silva (spikes), Remi dies, Jerrick kills Coburn, and Killian flees Greenstone with Silva's assets.
95.name: Mr Sparrow (Lawrence), Silva's kidnapping plot

96.content: Carlos Quilido: gold-rank priest of the Healer, soul-trauma specialist, broad-shouldered and swarthy; examines Jason's soul with a gold-rank projection ritual (his own soul looks like a sparkly apple; Jason's looks like a dark star-sky with sunlight annihilating alien shapes). Later designs the procedure to free brainwashed Order of Redeeming Light members (Sophie's mother Melody, treated in Book 12). Joins the Earth expedition to study medicine. Says 'Better right than fast'.
96.name: Carlos Quilido

97.comment: Spirit Warrior, Defiant, and Jason's Bronze changes
97.content: After the star seed: Quest System -> Defiant (ignore rank-disparity resistance and aura suppression bonuses; more loot effect against higher-rank monsters; quests lost). Title Spirit Warrior (stronger aura suppression, can attack a suppressed soul directly). Path of Shadows at bronze: sense shadows, teleport without line of sight, and Shadow Gate (regional portal, 10-minute cooldown, previously visited destination, ~40 km range, 10 iron entities per gate). Hegemony bronze: enemies attacking allies in the aura receive unresistable Sin. Dread Salvation ascends to bronze. Midnight Eyes bronze: Sense Magic. Cloak of Night reflexively intercepts projectiles. Jason reaches Bronze rank late in the book (face 'less awful'), grows a beard; scars: thin chin scar, left eyebrow scar, long torso scar.
97.name: Spirit Warrior, Defiant, and Jason's Bronze changes

98.comment: Silva and Lamprey punished; Greenstone politics after Ventress
98.content: Clarissa Ventress dies mysteriously; Darnell (leonid bodyguard) leads her organisation. Silva and Lamprey receive skeletal suppression (suppression inscribed onto the skeleton; permanent power loss; the Healer's church opposes); Silva returns to Greenstone, Lamprey to his birth city. Pochard Finn becomes acting Magic Society director. Jason advises the Duke of Greenstone (personable) to take control of the Old City and make Adris Dorgan official mayor. Jason threatens Elizabeth Silva to stop gang violence. Jerrick and Dean are reinstated.
98.name: Silva and Lamprey punished; Greenstone politics after Ventress

99.content: Jason, alone, kills ~two dozen bandits (ex-Silva/Ventress essence users who took a town and traded slaves to northern nomads) with stealth, Punition and Verdict; Colin's first execution via leech explosion; Jason is troubled by how little it troubles him. Arabelle secretly shadows him and warns him not to consider himself equal to elite iron-rankers. Guide: local hunter Keith.
99.name: Veldt Bandit Contract

100.comment: Order of the Reaper astral space - the Builder's boarding vessel
100.content: The Reaper-trials astral space is artificial: a giant boarding vessel of the Builder, ringed by 12 portal towers (8 km apart), each holding a dormant diamond-rank world engineer golem, with a central tower. The Order of the Reaper repurposed its delivery system into a portal system using Jason-like power. Clive's plan: carry an inversion device up the central tower to burn out the world engineers and power a portal home. The cult builds a beacon, then a real astral tunnel, and a 100 m stone ring gate lowers cultists in blue light. The Builder's side: converted clergy with clockwork cores, spyder drones, energy ghoul. After Clive's inversion the astral space slowly drifts away as a transcendent vehicle.
100.name: Order of the Reaper astral space - the Builder's boarding vessel

101.content: Zato: silver-rank cult leader who becomes an unkillable metal-skinned zealot (silver second skin, crystal eyes, explodes and reforms); shattered by Sophie with Hero's Moment, Deny the Reaper and a gold spirit coin. Timos: snide embedded cultist who cultivated Landemere Vane; branded 'sin' by Jason's Castigate; flees. Dougall (Cressida's servant) is ascended to silver and used as the Builder's first vessel, then discarded as an 'energy ghoul' that eats souls. The Builder then takes Thadwick Mercer's body.
101.name: Zato and Timos (Builder cult leaders)

102.content: Archbishop Nicolas Hendren (Herston in some notes): low-mid silver Purity leader with a wooden rune staff, barrier dome, mana-crystallising and passive cleansing; made a pact with the Builder cult. Killed by Jason with Feast of Absolution and Verdict after crying 'Lord! Why can you not speak to me?'; Jason: 'your lord is a bit of a prick'. His storage shows documents proving a church-cult agreement.
102.name: Archbishop Nicolas Hendren

103.content: In Book 3 Anisa Lasalle (bronze, Purity priestess) is knowingly allied with the Builder cult; Humphrey kills her in one blow with Flying Leap and Giant's Might after Stash distracts her and Hendren shoves her aside.
103.name: Anisa Lasalle - death

104.content: The Builder (a great astral being) acts through human vessels: first Dougall, then Thadwick Mercer (with Builder star-seed power given to nobles only), whose body it hollows out. Calls Jason 'Rejector'. Jason mocks him as 'Bill', 'intergalactic brickie'. In the final battle the Builder collars Jason (suppression collar), Jason impales himself on a spike wall and tackles the Builder from the tower window; the team completes the inversion. The Builder's vessel Thadwick's remnant becomes an energy vampire.
104.name: The Builder possesses Thadwick Mercer

105.comment: Death of Jason (Book 3) and the World-Phoenix Token
105.content: Jason dies (stone spike through the neck) at the end of Book 3: 'You have died. [World-Phoenix Token] has been consumed.' His body becomes rainbow smoke (like a monster) and he is returned to Earth, appearing on Earth in Book 4. In Interstice, the World-Phoenix (celestine vessel: alabaster skin, ruby hair, red gem eyes), Reaper (through Velius) and Builder (through Shako) negotiate: the Builder may not interfere with Earth (no star seeds/tokens/vessels, unmake unused ones); Jason receives no more resurrections but may accept a power; Reaper adds another outworlder companion (Gary/Farrah, trusted and knowledgeable).
105.name: Death of Jason (Book 3) and the World-Phoenix Token

106.content: Interstice: oldest, largest city-world, flat plane at the centre of the cosmos; only diamond-rankers enter freely; contains great astral beings' districts (Builder's, Reaper's), the island region Glim (rainbow ice), Fueros (World-Phoenix region: red/yellow crystal spires). Peripheral universes feed gold-rankers into it. Boris Ketland has visited; Jason has not yet.
106.name: Interstice

107.content: Shako: pale, freckled, red-haired, green-eyed diamond-ranker servant of the Builder; his world's imperial dynasty was given golems by the Builder; he refused to help his descendants and saved the empress and children as farmers. Later kills Jason in a battle (first appears Book 3; Book 6 Jason dies at Shako's hand in Earth timeline).
107.name: Shako

108.content: Velius: celestine with dark skin and silver curly hair; servant of the Reaper in Interstice; negotiates for the Reaper (who values Jason for freeing trapped souls). Shade is called the Reaper's most independent 'child'.
108.name: Velius

109.content: Dawn: celestine diamond-ranker (alabaster skin, ruby hair), centuries-old First Servant/First Sister of the Cult of the World-Phoenix; vessel in a snow-globe cottage; mentors Jason on Earth (taught him astral magic) and travels with him; later Dawn is also a recurring name. Helsveth: draconian (red/gold scales), second sister, diamond before 40, carried a star seed more than half her life; becomes the next First Sister. Dawn explains the Builder replaced the previous Builder, who meddled with universe seeds writing patterns into two seeds that became Earth and Pallimustus; the new Builder enabled a deity to build a link siphoning magic from Pallimustus to Earth, delaying the monster surge; the World-Phoenix strengthened Pallimustus's membrane.
109.name: Dawn (First Servant of the World-Phoenix)

110.content: Epilogue 5: In Melbourne, Detective Sergeant Adam Cosgrove (31) investigates a spherical hole where Jason's apartment vanished; federal cover-up; he is fired; Jason's sister Erika Asano (celebrity chef) tells him of a conspiracy (deaths by 'accident'/suicide). Miranda (super-strong, suited) and Dash (American, pastel shirt) recruit him: their organisation is preparing for the day the secret magic world is revealed. Used in Book 4.
110.name: Earth - Jason's disappearance (Book 3 epilogue)

111.content: Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller: 16 generations of Geller adventurers. In Book 3 his Attack of the Mirage Dragon evolves into Hero's Sacrifice (sacrifice health to enhance special attacks; backlash). Reaches bronze: Dragon Armour, Dragon Wings, Dragon Blood, Wing Raider, Unstoppable, Relentless Assault, Fire Breath, Dive Bomb, Shield Breaker, Unstoppable Force, Immortality, Spirit Reaper.
111.name: Humphrey Geller - Book 3 growth

112.content: Clive reaches bronze (Karmic abilities complete, amber light, body becomes tall and attractive). Staff Spell Lance of the Magister and wand Magister's Tithe (legendary set). Wrath of the Magister (prismatic beam or void sphere; colour effects Red heat, Yellow cost, Pink resist down, Green self-poison, Purple mana-harm, Orange more damage, Blue cold). Tools of the Magister, Juxtapose (swap), Rune Trap, Rune Gate (full portal + storage), Vengeance Mirror, Mantle of Retribution. Onslow is bronze (Beetle-sized, flies, elemental runes).
112.name: Clive Standish - Book 3 growth

113.content: Neil reaches bronze (hair fell out, golem sleeker). Abilities: Absorbing Shield, Burst Shield, Life Guard, Reaper's Redoubt, Bolster, Chrysalis Golem, Reels of Fortune, Cornucopia, Clean Slate, Grand Renewal (ritual-based big heal), Life Bolt, Hero's Moment, Eyes of Opportunity (see vulnerabilities).
113.name: Neil Davone - Book 3 growth

114.content: Sophie reaches bronze; celestine Astral Affinity evolves to Boundary Breaker (ignore rank-disparity resistances and aura suppression; more dimensional/transcendent damage). Karmic Warrior, Deny the Reaper, Wind Blade widens, Avatar of Speed. Belinda reaches bronze: Power Lock (curse), Pit of the Reaper, Force Tether, Instant Adept (wall/water running), Counterfeit Combatant, Specious Sorcerer (force bolt + life bolt), Unexpected Allies, Gemini and Shimmer (silver lantern).
114.name: Sophie and Belinda - Book 3 growth

115.comment: Valkyrie Match, Sigrid Freyn and Hastor
115.content: Sigrid Freyn: blond blue-eyed Valkyrie, healer-spearwoman, daughter of Hastor (gold-rank protocol officer of the Mirror King's court); on Valdis's team (Valdis: Master confluence from sword/swift/adept). Jason's team beats them in the last mirage match; Mirror King (late-30s looking, blond-bearded) and Hastor collect Valdis.
115.name: Valkyrie Match, Sigrid Freyn and Hastor

116.content: Gilbert Bertinelli (one of the octuplet Berts) becomes an essence user (iron, then more), barrel-chested and younger-looking; makes Jason's wardrobe in Vitesse style (Constance advised) and the Dark Hydra Robe (bronze epic: umbral snake + marsh hydra leather + deep wyrm silk lining). Bertram 'Bert' Bertinelli (silver, handsome, huge hammer) was Elspeth's secret protector. Albert promoted to 5th-floor desk.
116.name: Gilbert Bertinelli and Vitesse-style clothes

117.comment: Natalie and Padma's team (Vitesse Remore Academy graduates)
117.content: Vitesse team of Remore Academy graduates: Lance (elf leader, sword/myriad/adept = Master), Padma Parsell (smoulder, mentored by Farrah, same essences as Farrah), Oscar (celestine healer), Maximilian (draconian, dark green-purple scales, dislikes 'false dragon' Humphrey), Natalie (leonid female, stealth/disguise; befriends Belinda).
117.name: Natalie and Padma's team (Vitesse Remore Academy graduates)

118.content: BOOK 4: After dying in Book 3, Jason wakes naked and bald in the abandoned Casselton West Regional Hospital maternity theatre, on Earth, early June, ~18 months after he left (he left late November). A 'magic desolation' region (Earth's low magic) cuts his recovery, so he uses spirit coins. He gets Spirit Vault (Inventory evolves), title Indomitable, and the World-Phoenix offers Nirvanic Transfiguration (declined at first).
